title: PandaDoc Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Totals
summary: PandaDoc pricing runs $19 to $49 per user per month on annual billing, so you can work out exactly what your team costs.
body_markdown:
## Fix PandaDoc Handoffs With Activepieces


Activepieces, an open-source workflow automation tool with 744 integrations and an MIT-licensed core, can wire PandaDoc to your CRM, spreadsheet and chat, which may spare you a higher tier bought only for its native integrations.


It works around PandaDoc rather than inside it, and the saving depends on your plan's API access.


Run the cost-per-run math on the alternative. If a team upgrades a tier purely to get a built-in CRM sync, every seat pays for that connector, whether or not the seat ever touches it.


Pay an automation platform and you pay for the flow instead, so the cost follows the handoff and not the headcount.


Whether that's cheaper depends on one thing you must verify first: which PandaDoc plan exposes its API and webhooks. If those sit above your tier, the saving disappears, and you are back to pricing the tier that holds your workflow.


### Create PandaDoc Documents From CRM Deal Stages


Start in the CRM, the system where your sales team tracks deals. When a deal moves to a stage such as "proposal," a flow can fire, pull the contact and amount, and create a PandaDoc document from a template.


That removes the step where a rep re-types fields, which is where wrong figures and missing contacts usually enter a quote.


Pay once, in setup, and the flow works only as well as your template's field mapping, so the cost is not repeated on every document.


### Send signed status to the CRM and team


The return trip matters as much. When PandaDoc reports a document as completed, a second flow can update the deal, write a row to a spreadsheet, and post to a team channel.


Below, a screenshot shows the shape of such a flow in Activepieces: a Stripe "Payment Failed" trigger feeding a Slack "Send Message To A Channel" action. The run details report the first step as completed, with a "Run succeeded" notice at the bottom.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


Swap in a PandaDoc status change as the trigger and the same shape holds at any length: a two-step workaround and a ten-step flow for the deal, the sheet and the channel both cost 1 credit a run on Activepieces, as its pricing page states.


A meter that counts tasks, as Zapier's does, charges more the more carefully you split the handoff, which taxes the builder for doing it properly; here the run is the meter, and the steps inside it are free to multiply.


### What this does not replace


Do not expect Activepieces to replace PandaDoc's editor, signing, or audit features, or to grant API access your plan withholds.


It also adds a system to maintain: someone owns the flows, the credentials and the failures, and on the free plan's 1,000 credits a month, flows wait for the next day's credits once those run out.


Price that ownership honestly, then compare it against the tier upgrade. If the upgrade buys only the integration, automation is the cheaper route; if it also adds approvals or other features your workflow needs, you pay for the tier regardless.
